humanities_role_explanation: Topics such as TV shows & movies, Art, History, Music supply question content, but the competence tested is general persistent web browsing and information search, not humanities disciplinary skill.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Text-only questions with short text answers; the paper notes future benchmarks could cover images, video, audio, or interactive webpages.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Hard fact-seeking questions with a single short answer requiring persistent browsing, matching multiple constraints (inverted questions), 'reasoning about factuality' and multi-hop search; calibration error is also measured via model-stated confidence.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Scoped to one capability: persistent web browsing to find hard-to-find facts; the authors call it an incomplete but useful benchmark.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: GPT-4o, GPT-4o with browsing, GPT-4.5, OpenAI o1, and OpenAI Deep Research.

quantitative_metrics.note: Accuracy, calibration error, pass rates, voting-based accuracy.

summary: BrowseComp is a benchmark of 1,266 human-written, hard-to-find but easy-to-verify fact-seeking questions for browsing agents. Evaluation of OpenAI models shows near-zero accuracy for non-browsing models and 51.5% for Deep Research, with analyses of calibration, test-time compute scaling and aggregation.
key_findings: GPT-4o 0.6%, GPT-4o w/ browsing 1.9%, GPT-4.5 0.9%, o1 9.9%, Deep Research 51.5% accuracy. Browsing models have higher calibration error (Deep Research 91%). Accuracy scales smoothly with test-time compute; voting/best-of-N improve performance by 15-25%. Humans solved 29.2% of problems within two hours.
facets_explanation: The dataset was collected purely by human trainers who wrote inverted questions with single, indisputable short answers, following SimpleQA instructions. Trainers were asked to ensure no other valid answers existed and feedback was given if a second trainer found alternatives, and 21 tasks with ambiguous or incorrect labels were removed. Answers require external web knowledge not in the question. Grading uses an LLM comparing against the single reference string.
results_explanation: Table 3 reports 'Deep Research 51.5' accuracy as best, versus 'GPT-4o 0.6' without browsing. The format gap is an input/tool-access comparison (browsing vs. not); the largest gap, Deep Research vs GPT-4o without browsing, is about 51 points, but the models differ, so the figure of 50 is approximate and ambiguous as a same-model comparison. Humans solved 367/1,255 (29.2%), which is a solve rate under a give-up rule rather than the same metric, so human_gap_points is null.

plurality_treatment.quote: if another trainer found valid answers within ten minutes that was not the reference answer, feedback was given to trainers for them to revise their question.
